It also updates InstSimplify tests to expect poison results from constant propagation.
Changed symbols: llvm::ConstantFoldBinaryInstruction; ConstantFoldGetElementPtr; PoisonValue::get; insertelement_undef; overflow_fptosi
Behavioral change: Constant folding now treats several previously-undef results as poison.; Inbounds GEP folding now returns poison instead of undef when the base pointer choice would be out-of-bounds.; Constant-propagation tests were updated to reflect poison semantics.

Reproducer link: small -O1 crash involving constant folding and floating-point representability
Pass or subsystem link: llvm/lib/IR/ConstantFold.cpp; llvm/test/Transforms/InstSimplify

top_candidates.subject: [LowerConstantIntrinsics] reuse isManifestLogic from ConstantFolding
top_candidates.diff_summary:

top_candidates.subject: [InstSimplify] Properly constrain {insert,extract}_subvector intrinsic fold
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit tightens InstSimplify’s folding rule for the {insert,extract}_subvector intrinsic pair. The code now only folds an insert/extract chain to the original vector when the inserted vector is either the same value being extracted or undef, and the tests were updated to preserve non-redundant cases where the inserted vector differs. The substantive change is a narrower simplification precondition, not a new floating-point or APFloat-related transformation.
Changed symbols: simplifyIntrinsic; llvm.experimental.vector.extract; llvm.experimental.vector.insert; non_redundant_extract_insert_chain; non_redundant_extract_insert_chain_0; non_redundant_extract_insert_chain_1
Behavioral change: Adds an explicit constraint that the inserted vector operand must be either the extracted source vector or undef before folding the intrinsic chain.; Prevents InstSimplify from incorrectly collapsing semantically non-redundant vector insert/extract sequences.; Preserves the original IR when the insert source differs from the extracted vector.

Summary: This commit updates X86 SLP vectorizer cost-model tests for floating-point-to-integer vector conversions, especially fptoui patterns across SSE/AVX/AVX512 feature sets. The retrieved hunks show test expectation changes for vectorized fptoui/fptosi combinations and AVX512F gating, indicating cost-model or legalization behavior changes for vector FP conversion profitability and target feature selection. The visible evidence is test-only in the retrieved hunks, but it is directly in the floating-point conversion area.
Changed symbols: fptoui_8f32_8i64; fptoui_8f64_8i64; fptoui_8f64_8i32; fptoui_8f32_8i32; fptosi_fptoui; SLPVectorizer

top_candidates.subject: [Matrix] Remove unused matrix-propagate-shape option.
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This change simplifies LowerMatrixIntrinsics by removing the EnableShapePropagation option and making shape propagation unconditional. The pass now always seeds a worklist from matrix intrinsics and iterates forward/backward propagation until convergence.
Changed symbols: EnableShapePropagation; LowerMatrixIntrinsics; propagateShapeForward; propagateShapeBackward; WorkList
Behavioral change: Removes a conditional gate around shape propagation, so the propagation loop always runs.; Preserves the same propagation algorithm but changes when it is enabled: from opt-in/flag-controlled to always-on.; Potentially increases the amount of matrix-shape inference performed during lowering.
Assertion or trace link: APFloat; ConstantFold; getSemantics().isRepresentableBy; EarlyCSE
Reproducer link: clang crashes at -O1 on a very small C testcase
Pass or subsystem link: llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LowerMatrixIntrinsics.cpp
Causal explanation: This commit affects a scalar transform pass, but the retrieved hunk is specifically about matrix intrinsic shape propagation, not floating-point constant folding or APFloat representability. While it changes optimization behavior, there is no evidence here that it would trigger the reported ConstantFold/APFloat assertion. The connection to the issue is therefore weak and indirect at best.
Causal confidence: 0.14
Build risk: Optimization-pass behavior change; Could alter IR shape and downstream optimization opportunities; No direct overlap with the reported APFloat/ConstantFold assertion path

top_candidates.subject: [ConstantFolding] Use APFloat for constant folding. NFC
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This patch refactors ConstantFolding to use APFloat values directly in several floating-point folding paths instead of converting through primitive doubles/floats first. It changes math-lib no-op detection, scalar call folding for pow and floating-point intrinsics, and the ConstantFoldFP helper signature to operate on APFloat semantics-preserving inputs.
Changed symbols: llvm::isMathLibCallNoop; ConstantFoldScalarCall2; ConstantFoldScalarCall3; ConstantFoldFP; APFloat::copySign; minnum; maxnum; minimum
Behavioral change: Preserves and propagates APFloat semantics during constant folding instead of narrowing to host double/float conversions first.; Changes folding of floating-point intrinsics and math calls to use APFloat-based operations, which can affect representability checks and exact constant results.; Updates ConstantFoldFP to accept const APFloat& rather than a double, reducing loss of precision/semantics in folding decisions.
Assertion or trace link: APFloat; ConstantFold; getSemantics().isRepresentableBy; floating point; assertion
Reproducer link: clang crashes at -O1; small C testcase; constant folding during optimization
Pass or subsystem link: llvm/lib/Analysis/ConstantFolding.cpp; constant folding
Causal explanation: This commit directly touches the subsystem named in the issue and changes how floating-point constants are folded and represented. Because the crash involves an APFloat/ConstantFold representability assertion, moving from double-based folding to APFloat-based folding is plausibly related: it can change whether a value is considered representable and thus whether the assertion is triggered or avoided. The retrieved hunks do not prove the exact failing path, but they provide strong subsystem-level evidence.
Causal confidence: 0.91
